_comment: RQ-001 — behavior-surfaces-as-code. The single source of truth for which changed paths are BEHAVIOR-BEARING, i.e. must select a paid behavioral/routing evaluation before they merge. plugin_behavior_paths drive the per-plugin behavioral (promptfoo) leg: ${plugin} is substituted with the matrix plugin name, and the same strings must appear verbatim (with ${plugin} -> '${{ matrix.plugin }}') in the behavioral-run paths-filter in .github/workflows/evals.yml. routing_paths drive the roster routing leg the same way. ci/check_behavior_surfaces.py asserts, offline, that (a) this spec and the workflow filters are in verbatim lockstep both directions, and (b) a deterministic counterfeit table of changed-file cases — including behavior edits OUTSIDE SKILL.md — selects exactly the packs it should. Widening or narrowing a trigger is therefore a deliberate two-file edit the cheap tier notices, never silent drift. Guard scripts (skills/**/scripts/**) are deliberately ABSENT here: they are the deep tier's frozen surface (ci/required-checks.json deep_safety_paths), not the behavioral tier's. The root AGENTS.md is also deliberately absent: it is repo governance at the marketplace root, outside every plugin's source dir, and is never shipped by an install (ci/install-smoke.sh walks marketplace source -> plugin dir -> declared components) — an all-legs trigger for it would be exactly the spurious paid spend RQ-001's acceptance criteria forbid. HONEST LIMIT: selection guarantees the matching pack RUNS; it does not put the changed file into that pack's prompt — packs today inject SKILL.md, so making each pack inject its other triggering surfaces is behavioral-pack design, tracked under the testing-strategy work (issue #89), not this trigger map.
